text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Conflict between Amsterdam Exchanges and some smaller investment banks over new order processing rules. (p1)
- CD producer Docdata is expecting strong growth after buying two British Mayking units. (p1)
- Schiphol Airport plans to introduce a ban on night flights from today. (p1)
- Philips Electronics to continue cost-cutting programme for several more years. (p3)
- Dutch farmers refuse to pay back excess EU subsidies. (p5)
- Investors miss out on last week's capital gain on Multihouse shares as Bank Labouchere sells them to prospective buyer of the automation company. (p2)
- Music and film producer PolyGram takes matters at Motown unit in hand. (p2)
- U.S. toy giant Hasbro in conflict with Dutch rival Impag over copies of their products. (p2)
- Fashion shop chain The Society Shop is slowly on its way to get on top of things again. (p21)
- Petrol stations start a collective fund to cover any future claims for pollution at their sites. (p21)
- Dairy cooperative Coberco in legal fight over redundancies at the beginning of this year. (p7)
- Consumer organisation says it is impossible to convert from guilder to euro in a week. (p7)
